vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: has-anonymizer
Version: 1.0.0

The has-anonymizer skill bundle provides a comprehensive on-device privacy toolset for text and image anonymization. The code demonstrates high security standards, including path traversal protections in both `has_image.py` and `has_text.py` (via `_is_within_directory` checks), and the use of restricted file permissions (0600) when saving sensitive mapping files in `mapping.py`. The bundle manages a local `llama-server` instance for text processing and uses YOLO11 for image segmentation, with all logic focused on its stated purpose of privacy protection. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill is broadly coherent with an on-device text/image anonymizer, but there are implementation and configuration mismatches (undeclared environment variables, model download vs runtime paths, and ability to talk to non-local servers) that could lead to unintended data flow or confusion.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (text/image anonymization) maps to the files and runtime requirements: text code drives a local llama-server model and image code uses ultralytics/YOLO. Declared required binaries (llama-server, uv), brew install of llama.cpp and uv, and model downloads from HuggingFace are appropriate for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the included scripts keep to anonymization and scanning tasks. However, the text runtime can inspect local processes (lsof/ps), start/stop a local llama-server, and -- importantly -- will use whatever server_url it is given: if configured with a non-loopback URL the client/server code will contact remote endpoints. That means anonymization/restoration requests could be routed off-device if a remote server is configured. The README asserts 'entirely on-device' but the code permits remote servers; this is a scope deviation worth noting.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install steps use Homebrew formulas (llama.cpp, uv) and model downloads from huggingface.co (explicit URLs). These are standard release hosts; no arbitrary shorteners or unknown personal servers. The skill relies on Python packages (ultralytics, opencv-python-headless, pillow, requests) but relies on 'uv' to run/manage them rather than bundling arbitrary executables.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill metadata declares no required env vars, but runtime code reads environment variables (e.g., HAS_IMAGE_MODEL, HAS_TEXT_MODEL_PATH / HAS_TEXT_MODEL) to locate models. Those env vars are not documented in requires.env. This is an inconsistency: absent or unexpected env vars could silently alter behavior (point model paths to arbitrary files), and a misconfigured server URL environment could send data off-device. No cloud credentials are requested, which is appropriate, but the undeclared env var usage is a red flag.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not declared always: true and is user-invocable. It writes models and mappings into local paths (defaults under ~/.openclaw/tools/has-anonymizer/models and /tmp log files) and may start a local llama-server bound to loopback ports. It does not request system-wide persistent privileges or modify other skills. Mapping files are handled with restrictive file permissions (0600), which is good.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement an on-device anonymizer, but before installing you should: (1) confirm you are comfortable installing brew packages (llama.cpp, uv) and the listed Python deps (ultralytics, opencv, pillow, requests) via uv; (2) verify the model download URLs are valid and that you or the installer place the downloaded models where the code expects them — note the install metadata downloads into a 'models' directory, but the code defaults to ~/.openclaw/tools/has-anonymizer/models (fixing this mismatch or setting HAS_IMAGE_MODEL / HAS_TEXT_MODEL_PATH may be necessary); (3) be aware that the code can be pointed at a non-local llama-server (remote URL) — if you or your environment configures a remote server, sensitive mapping data or text could be sent off-device; (4) mapping files can completely reverse anonymization, so keep those JSON files protected (they set 0600 permissions by default); and (5) the runtime inspects local processes (lsof/ps) and will start/stop a local server and bind to ports — check for port conflicts and review /tmp/llama-server-*.log if starting the server. If you want to reduce risk: run everything in an isolated environment (VM/container), ensure server_url remains loopback, and explicitly set HAS_*_MODEL paths to trusted local files.
